clue.text: Labour politician tours island nation

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so the politician's name goes round the island letter

parts.note: Tony Benn was a leading Labour politician

explanation.surface: A Labour MP goes on a trip round an island country.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn was a prominent figure in Britain's Labour Party for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a sovereign country in West Africa, bordering Nigeria and Togo.

clue.text: Kenneth, he really every so often displays charm

indicators.note: every so often means at intervals, so alternate letters are taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Kenneth, he periodically really does show charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or spellbind, which is what charming someone does.

clue.text: One getting a lewd instinct about Jedward possibly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means around and here in a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets a rude urge regarding the pop duo Jedward.
explanation.walkthrough: Jedward are John and Edward Grimes, Irish twin brothers who found fame on The X Factor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jedward are an example of twins from one fertilised egg who look exactly alike.

clue.text: Son sculpted female figure, not half intimidating

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: not half says only the first half of the word is kept, its second half dropped

parts.note: a caryatid is a carved stone woman used as a column in classical architecture

explanation.surface: A son carved a statue of a woman that was menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: CARYATID has eight letters; 'not half' keeps the first four, CARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scary frightens people, which is what being intimidating means.

clue.text: Hairstyle that's cropped barely becomes widespread

parts.note: corn is grown and cropped, i.e. harvested

indicators.note: barely means stripped bare, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: grows means spreads or increases

explanation.surface: A haircut that is closely trimmed hardly catches on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' looks like 'hardly', but it means bared: GROWS without its outer letters gives ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornrows are hair braided flat to the scalp in tight parallel lines, a style of braiding.

clue.text: Apologetic parent, wrong to gobble peanuts regularly

indicators.note: to gobble is to swallow, so the rearranged letters take the others inside
wrong means incorrect, so the letters of parent are put in a different order
regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter of peanuts is taken

explanation.surface: A sorry parent, who shouldn't eat peanuts in a routine way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone repentant feels sorry for wrongdoing, which is what being apologetic expresses.

clue.text: TV's Oscar with chronic fatigue, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals sound, so the two letters said aloud, em-ee, give the answer

parts.note: ME (myalgic encephalomyelitis) is chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: A television award winner suffering from chronic tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's top award, as the Oscar is cinema's.

clue.text: Old hotel tonight mistaken about number turning up

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other part
mistaken means wrong, so the letters of hotel tonight are rearranged
turning up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed

explanation.surface: An elderly hotel guest got the room number wrong this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HOTEL TONIGHT goes about ON, which is NO turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Long in the tooth is an idiom for elderly, from horses' gums receding with age.

clue.text: Smooth, extremely atypical variety of footwear

parts.note: to sand is to smooth a surface with sandpaper

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of atypical are kept

explanation.surface: An untypical sort of shoe that is extremely sleek.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is an open shoe with straps, one kind of shoe among many.

clue.text: Standard terms are being modified

indicators.note: letters that are being modified are changed in order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The usual conditions of a contract are being revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as an adjective for the terms, but it is the noun for a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and a streamer is a long narrow pennant flown the same way.

clue.text: Drug for unknown adult having cold

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
Z is one of the algebraic unknowns x, y, z
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A medicine meant for an unnamed grown-up who has a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is the brand name of fluoxetine, a widely prescribed antidepressant medicine.

clue.text: Bubbly female mostly undecided over hubby after vacation

indicators.note: over in an across clue says the shortened word is turned back to front
mostly says most of the word is used, its final letter cut

parts.note: torn, as in torn between two choices, means undecided

indicators.note: after vacation the word hubby is emptied of its inside, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A woman, unsure about her husband once their holiday ends, is giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' looks like a time phrase, but it means hubby is vacated: HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a liquid full of foam, and also a light, lively manner.

clue.text: Turncoat angered volatile European

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so the letters of angered are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traitor angered a hot-tempered man from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat deserts their side for the enemy, and a renegade is exactly such a deserter.

clue.text: German agreed to visit rugby player with tetanus

indicators.note: the German word comes to visit, placed straight after the rugby player

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
ja is German for yes, the word said when agreeing

explanation.surface: A German agreed to go and see a rugby player who had tetanus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the everyday name for tetanus, whose first symptom is spasm of the jaw muscles.

clue.text: Wood Jack Lovelace maybe roughly managed to cut

parts.note: J is the playing-card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so the two short pieces go into the name

parts.note: Ada Lovelace was the nineteenth-century mathematician, an example of an Ada
ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Jack and Ada Lovelace roughly cut some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Ada Lovelace, Byron's daughter, is credited as the first computer programmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacaranda is a tropical tree whose hard fragrant timber is used for furniture.

clue.text: Pupil, unnamed, goes round boxing rings

indicators.note: goes round says the hidden letters are read in reverse order
boxing means enclosing, so the answer is held inside the words Pupil unnamed

explanation.surface: An anonymous schoolchild is circling a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pupil unnamed' backwards: DEMANNULIPUP, and the answer sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the plural of annulus, the geometric term for a ring-shaped region between two circles.

clue.text: Typically French plant gets left for source of roughage

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the L takes the place of the other letter

parts.note: garlic is a plant of the onion family

indicators.note: source of means the first letter, where the word roughage starts

explanation.surface: A plant like garlic acquires fibre for a healthy diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic relates to Gaul, the old name for France, so it describes something characteristic of the French.

clue.text: Drive from harbour, heading off requiring fuel essentially

indicators.note: heading off means losing its head, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or sheltered anchorage

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or core, so the middle letters of fuel are taken

explanation.surface: Drive from a port, needing petrol above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a road, as in a street name.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and avenue are both words for a road, especially a broad tree-lined street.

clue.text: One promoting game perhaps that's comparatively tough

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a meat seller, who may sell game such as pheasant or venison
second meaning: more butch, the comparative of butch, meaning tough and macho

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a sport being advertised; it is game birds or animals on a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a meat trader and the comparative adjective of butch, meaning more rugged.

clue.text: Doctor believed Spain disregarded plague

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged
disregarded means left out, so the Spanish letter is set aside from the pool

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (Espana)

explanation.surface: A doctor trusted that Spain ignored an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from BELIEVED, leaving BLIEVED, and rearrange that. 'plague' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or harass persistently, which is what plague means as a verb.

clue.text: Proceeds from eastern location, south of Cromer, ultimately

indicators.note: south of in a down clue says these pieces come below, i.e. after, the letter
ultimately means at last, so the final letter of Cromer is taken

parts.note: Cromer is a seaside town on the Norfolk coast in eastern England
a venue is a location where an event is held

explanation.surface: Takings from a site on England's east coast, south of the town of Cromer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromer is a resort town in Norfolk, East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, the money that comes in, as proceeds from a sale do.

clue.text: Dvorak symphony recognised on radio by the public

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is used for how it sounds

parts.note: knew means recognised, as in knew someone by sight
the world, as in all the world can see, means people at large

explanation.surface: A Dvorak symphony that listeners know from broadcasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvorak's Symphony No. 9, From the New World, is commonly known by its subtitle.

clue.text: Case of fruit four tucked into

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the numeral goes inside the fruit

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A box of fruit that four people have eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads as eating, but it means put inside. 'Case' is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case marking the indirect object, in Latin or German for example.

clue.text: Dim banker undermines deputy at first

indicators.note: undermines in a down clue says the river goes under, i.e. after, the letter
at first means the opening letter, so only the start of deputy is used

parts.note: a banker is a crossword word for a river, something with banks; the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A dim-witted banker who undercuts the deputy first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, something that has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the darker stage of twilight, and as an adjective it means shadowy or gloomy.

clue.text: Enter side road briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a turning is a side road branching off a main road

explanation.surface: Go into a minor road for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is to go in, as when a driver turns into a driveway, or to hand something over.

clue.text: Very small number welcoming current peer

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the other letters take in the current

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to count is to number, as in to number the votes
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A tiny figure greets a nobleman of the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a verb here: count. 'current' looks like an adjective for the peer but is electric current, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a nobleman ranking between an earl and a baron, so a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Smart coats some men put on dogs

definitions.text: Smart coats some men put on
definitions.meaning: first meaning: tailcoats, worn by men at formal events
second meaning: follows closely, a verb, as a detective dogs a suspect

explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' looks like a noun, as if men dress up dogs; it is the verb to shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means formal evening dress with tailcoats, and as a verb it means to shadow someone secretly.

clue.text: Applaud old driver quelling a public disturbance

indicators.note: quelling a riot means putting it down, so those letters are suppressed and removed

parts.note: a charioteer drove a chariot in ancient times, like Ben-Hur
a riot is a violent disturbance of the peace in public

explanation.surface: Praise an elderly motorist who stops a street riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to shout approval, as to applaud is to clap approval.
